questions.stem: An airplane begins its descent from a cruising altitude of 33,000 feet and descends at a constant rate of 1,800 feet per minute. Which of the following statements best describes how the plane’s distance from its cruising altitude changes over time?
choices: The plane’s distance from its cruising altitude is increasing linearly over time.
The plane’s distance from its cruising altitude is decreasing linearly over time.
The plane’s distance from its cruising altitude is increasing exponentially over time.
The plane’s distance from its cruising altitude is decreasing exponentially over time.
questions.verify: distance below cruising altitude = 1,800t: grows by a constant amount each minute

questions.stem: The sides of a rectangle are such that the length is 11 centimeters more than 8 times the width, in centimeters. If the width of the rectangle is 5 centimeters, what is the area, in square centimeters, of the rectangle?

The function f is defined by \(f(x)=(x-2)(x-8)(x+3)\). In the xy-plane, the graph of y = h(x) is the result of translating the graph of y = f(x) up 6 units. What is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of the graph of y = h(x)?

The function \(A(b)=7b^{2}\) gives the area of a right triangle, in square centimeters (\(\text{cm}^{2}\)), if the length of its base is b cm and the length of its height is 14 times the length of its base. Which of the following is the best interpretation of A(18) = 2,268?
choices: If the length of the base of the triangle is 2,268 cm, then the length of the height of the triangle is 18 cm.
If the length of the base of the triangle is 18 cm, then the length of the height of the triangle is 2,268 cm.
If the length of the base of the triangle is 18 cm, then the area of the triangle is 2,268 \(\text{cm}^{2}\).
If the length of the base of the triangle is 2,268 cm, then the area of the triangle is 18 \(\text{cm}^{2}\).

questions.stem: Circle N has a radius of 6 millimeters (mm). Circle M has an area of \(121\pi\ \text{mm}^{2}\). What is the total area, in \(\text{mm}^{2}\), of circles N and M?
Function f is defined as \(f(x)=(2x-5)^{2}\), and function g is defined as g(x) = 2(2x + 7). Which of the following is equivalent to f(x) + g(x)?
The figure shown is a right rectangular pyramid, where \(\ell=14\) units, w = 7 units, and h = 13 units. What is the surface area, in square units, of the pyramid?
questions.verify: base 98; slant heights √(13² + 3.5²) over ℓ and √(13² + 7²) over w
flags: Answer is not a whole number (≈389.83). Valid if h is the pyramid's height, as the right-angle mark shows; confirm against the source key.

questions.stem: The graph of the linear function y = f(x) − 19 is shown. If c and d are positive constants, which equation could define f?
questions.verify: graph through (-4, 0), (0, -7.5): f(x) = -15/8 x + 11.5, negative slope, positive intercept

questions.stem: \[50x=12{,}500y-10{,}000\]One of the two equations in a system of linear equations is given. The system has no solution. Which equation could be the second equation in this system?
questions.verify: sympy: A no solution, B and C one point, D infinitely many

questions.stem: The concentration of calcium, in milligrams per liter (mg/L), is found for three samples of water: bottled, tap, and mineral. The concentration of calcium in the sample of bottled water is 48% of the concentration of calcium in the sample of tap water and 24% of the concentration of calcium in the sample of mineral water. If the concentration of calcium in the sample of tap water is 36 mg/L, what is the concentration of calcium, in mg/L, in the sample of mineral water?

For a certain type of rope, the equation \(y=900ax^{2}\), where a is a constant, gives the estimated breaking strength y, in pounds, of a rope with a circumference of x inches. Based on this equation, if a rope of this type has a circumference of 0.75 inches, it has an estimated breaking strength of 708.75 pounds. What is the estimated breaking strength, in pounds, of a rope of this type that has a circumference of 4.50 inches?

A science club from a certain high school in Ohio conducted an experiment to study the effects of smell on taste. A sample of 100 students was selected at random from the high school to participate in the experiment. First, the students tasted a pureed food sample while wearing covered goggles and nose plugs. Then, the students tasted the same pureed food sample without nose plugs. 35 students were able to correctly identify the pureed food sample while wearing nose plugs. Which of the following is the largest population to which the results of the experiment can be generalized?
choices: All students from the high school
The 100 students who participated in the experiment
The 35 students who were able to correctly identify the pureed food sample while wearing nose plugs
All students from high schools in Ohio
questions.verify: random sample drawn from that one high school

questions.stem: The expression \(6x^{4}+17x^{2}+7\) can be rewritten as \((3x^{2}+a)(2x^{2}+b)\), where a and b are positive integers, or as \((3x^{2}+c)(2x^{2}+d)\), where c and d are positive nonintegers. What is the value of a + c?
questions.verify: sympy: (3x^2 + 7)(2x^2 + 1) so a = 7; nonintegers c = 3/2, d = 14/3; a + c = 8.5

questions.stem: The function f is a quadratic function. In the xy-plane, the graph of y = f(x) has a vertex at (1, 8) and passes through the points (2, 47) and (−1, 164). What is the value of f(−2) − f(0)?
\[f(x)=11x^{10}+3x^{8}\]\[g(x)=-15x^{7}+7x^{5}\]The polynomial p(x) is defined as the product of the given polynomials, f(x) and g(x). What is the coefficient of \(x^{15}\) in p(x)?
